title: Aperture Dynamics - time-to-first-token & deployment fit (Discovery)
next_steps: Redwood to send tailored quickstart playbook and sample prompt set by 2025-06-20
Customer to share representative latency-sensitive prompt set and 3-week pilot timeline by 2025-06-23
Schedule 1-hour dedicated runtime deep dive with engineering (Liam + Emily) week of 2025-06-23
action_items: Maya Chen: Email quickstart credits activation link and account on-boarding checklist; due 2025-06-20
Liam O'Connor: Prep micro-benchmark plan (latency & throughput) and example config for Aperture's short-context RLHF prompts; due 2025-06-22
Carlos Mendez: Share Aperture's SOC2 + encryption requirements doc with Redwood; due 2025-06-21
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
summary: Discovery with Aperture Dynamics focused on a fast PLG-style onramp (free credits, TTFT) plus evaluation criteria for scaling to Dedicated or Private. Customer cares about 75-150ms tail latency for short prompts, data residency and KMS integration, and clear pilot success metrics. Redwood to provide quickstart credits, a bench plan, and follow-up deep dive for runtime tuning.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya Chen from Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:08] Raj: Raj Patel, CTO at Aperture Dynamics, hi. We've got Emily, Carlos and Sofia here.
[00:15] Maya: Awesome. Liam from our infra team is on too — Liam, do you want to say hi?
[00:20] Liam: Hey all, Liam O'Connor, site reliability / inference runtime at Redwood. Happy to dig into perf details.
[00:27] Maya: Goal for today — figure out quickest path to first token for your team, and validate whether hosted is sufficient or you'll need Dedicated or Private. Also cover security gating. Should take ~30 minutes.
[00:39] Sofia: Sounds good. We have a hard timeline — product demo at the end of July and we'd like to have a pilot running in the next 3 weeks.
[00:46] Maya: Great, that helps. Raj, can you give a bit of context on current infra and what you're building?
[00:53] Raj: Sure. We're a startup building a multimodal search assistant for product catalogs. Latency is a key metric for the UX — 75 to 150ms median for short Q&A flows would be ideal. Right now we call OpenAI for embeddings and a couple of completions but cost is rising. We're looking for a more predictable unit cost and better control over private customer data.
[01:18] Emily: On the ML side we run a mix of small contextual prompts (~256 tokens) and a few longer rerank flows. We have strict PII handling and need KMS-backed encryption for any persistent KV cache.
[01:29] Carlos: Security-wise, we'd need SSO/SAML, audit logs, and SOC2 compliance. For Private option, HSM/KMS integration is non-negotiable.
[01:39] Liam: Totally understand. On the TTFT side, our PLG flow can get you to first token within a day — often within an hour if you use the SDK and sample prompt sets. Free credits help accelerate that. For the latency targets you mentioned, we'd want to run a micro-benchmark with representative prompts.
[01:56] Raj: When you say micro-benchmark, what exactly do you need from us?
[02:00] Liam: Ideally a small set of 10-20 representative requests, with the avg and worst-case seq lengths. We test hosted model variants, measure p95/p99, and then suggest either a dedicated pool config or quantization profile.
[02:14] Emily: Can you run those tests against our private model data or do we need to sanitize?
[02:19] Maya: For hosted trials, we recommend sanitized prompts if they contain PII. If you need raw data, Dedicated or Private is the right path — you can bring VPC peering or on-prem and we can orchestrate a pilot that never leaves your network.
[02:33] Carlos: Ok. What's the unit price delta between Hosted and Dedicated? We want to model cost.
[02:38] Maya: Hosted is usage-based per-token; Dedicated provides committed GPU pools with predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. Pricing is quote-based but for planning we can provide a sample amortized cost spreadsheet.
[02:50] Raj: Are there middle-ground options for caching and autoscaling? We want cost predictability but not overcommit.
[02:57] Liam: Yes — we support burst capacity on Dedicated and smart routing to cheaper model variants for non-critical routes. Also prefix/KV cache can dramatically reduce token costs for repetitive queries. We can show you a before/after with caching enabled.
[03:12] Sofia: How much work is the SDK integration? Our frontend is Node + Typescript.
[03:17] Maya: We have official SDKs for Node, Python, and Go. Example quickstart repo, sample serverless template, and a Postman collection. Time to first token for a developer is typically 15-60 minutes: create API key, pull example, run sample request.
[03:30] Raj: Nice. What's included in the free credits?
[03:32] Maya: Credits cover model usage and embeddings, a reserved block for up to 100k tokens and a couple of bench runs. We'll attach a quickstart playbook with step-by-step TTFT instructions and a guide to run the micro-bench.
[03:45] Emily: On benchmarks — does Redwood expose per-token latency breakdown so we can see KV cache vs generation cost?
[03:50] Liam: Yes, our Console has token-level latency and cost breakdowns, model-level tracing hooks, and per-request logs. For deeper analysis we'll share a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and an operator view of batch sizes and GPU utilization.
[04:05] Carlos: For SOC2 and SSO, do you support SCIM provisioning?
[04:09] Maya: We do SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We can share our compliance pack (SOC2 report, encryption at rest docs, KMS integrations) after NDA if needed.
[04:20] Carlos: We'll likely need the SOC2 evidence for our procurement.
[04:23] Maya: Understood. We'll include that in the follow-up.
[04:27] Sofia: If we start on Hosted and later want to move to Dedicated, how painful is that migration?
[04:32] Liam: It's designed to be smooth. The API contract is consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. You can pin model versions and rollout policies. Migration mostly involves provisioning dedicated GPU pools and configuring routing policies; we assist with model variant selection and can run canary traffic.
[04:48] Raj: Good. Can you support KMS for caching keys?
[04:52] Liam: For Dedicated and Private we support customer KMS/HSM. For Hosted, we offer managed key options but for strict compliance we usually recommend Private with customer-managed KMS.
[05:03] Emily: A technical question — how does Redwood handle KV cache and large context? We sometimes attach a product document store and don't want to re-tokenize too often.
[05:11] Liam: Our runtime supports prefix/KV caching and smart cache eviction. For large contexts we can configure sharded KV caches and prefetch heuristics. Also continuous batching reduces per-token compute. We'll need to see your sequence length distribution to recommend cache sizing.
[05:28] Raj: Any caveats around quantization? We run a custom model family and worry about quality regressions.
[05:33] Liam: We provide quantization profiles and quality monitoring. For model onboarding we run evals on your prompt set and threshold alerts for regressions. If quality drops, we can fallback to float16 variants.
[05:46] Maya: Quick note on pilot definition — typical success metrics are: TTFT under X for 80% requests, p95 under your target, and cost per request below your ceiling. We can agree on clear SLA-like pilot goals.
[05:58] Sofia: I like that. For the demo at the end of July we'll need about 1 week of stable pilot data. Can you get us to pilot in 3 weeks?
[06:07] Maya: Yes, with credits and a focused bench we can. Step 1 is activate credits and spin up a test API key. Step 2 run the micro-benchmark (we'll provide the script). Step 3 iterate on model variant and cache.
[06:20] Raj: Is there a templated playbook?
[06:22] Maya: Yes — TTFT playbook, bench script, and a migration runbook. We'll drop links in the follow-up.
[06:29] Emily: One last thing — we sometimes route to an internal reranker in our infra. Can we hybridize so embeddings stay on Redwood but reranker runs in our infra?
[06:38] Liam: Absolutely. You can mix calls — embeddings, generation, and rerankers can live wherever. Our routing policies support hybrid architectures. We'll show an example wiring diagram.
[06:49] Carlos: For procurement, ballpark SLA and support tiers?
[06:52] Maya: For Hosted PLG there's standard support; Dedicated/Private come with enterprise support and optional SLA. We'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[07:00] Raj: Ok thanks. Anything else from Redwood?
[07:03] Maya: We'll send: quickstart credits, playbook, benchmark script, compliance pack link (NDA if required), and schedule a runtime deep dive.
[07:12] Sofia: We'll also share our prompt sample and the exact latency targets. Expect Carlos to send the security doc.
[07:18] Maya: Great — recap and next steps?
[07:21] Liam: Action items: bench plan + config from me; credits and playbook from Maya; security doc from Carlos; schedule deep dive.
[07:29] Raj: Good meeting, thanks all.
[07:31] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday.
[07:35] [call ends]
